Official Illinois Courts sources were then read as independent corroboration of the rule-versus-form distinction; they confirm the in-repository mapping and are recorded as corroboration rather than as the controlling basis.

The official-source reading was a read, not an acquisition: nothing was deposited, no receipt was written and no repository binary changed. questionPresented: What does the repository identity 'Ill. S. Ct. R. 298 Application for Waiver of Court Fees' name — a rule, a form, or both — and is the source behind it correctly bound?

rule298Treatment.whatRule298Governs: Applications for waiver of court fees, costs and charges in a civil action under 735 ILCS 5/5-105, together with the filing, decision, document-retention and civil-legal-services-certification procedure for such applications.
rule298Treatment.sourceClassBasis: The rule contains no fillable application. It directs the applicant to a separately approved form: 'An applicant shall use the "Application for Waiver of Court Fees" form approved by the Illinois Supreme Court and the Supreme Court Commission on Access to Justice, which includes a certification under 735 ILCS 5/1-109.' A rule that names a form is not that form.
rule298Treatment.currentRuleTitle: Rule 298. Application for Waiver of Court Fees, Costs, and Charges
rule298Treatment.amendingOrder: M.R. 3140, order entered 2023-05-30, effective 2023-09-01, amending Illinois Supreme Court Rules 298 and 404
rule298Treatment.creditLineVerbatim: Amended October 20, 2003, effective November 1, 2003; amended September 25, 2014, eff. immediately; amended Dec. 29, 2017, eff. Jan. 1, 2018; amended Feb. 13, 2019, eff. July 1, 2019; amended May 30, 2023, eff. Sept. 1, 2023.
rule298Treatment.priorRuleTitle: Rule 298. Application to Sue or Defend as an Indigent Person
rule298Treatment.priorRuleTitleBasis: an archived official illinoiscourts.gov Article II capture dated 2017-01-06; the rule was renamed by the 2014 amendment and again by the 2023 amendment
rule298Treatment.scopeOfTheRule: civil actions generally; not limited to particular proceedings
rule298Treatment.reachesExpungementAndSealingBasis: Rule 298's own text does not name expungement or 20 ILCS 2630/5.2. The routing is established by the official statewide expungement instructions ATJ 2900.10 (06/26), 'How To Clear Your Criminal Record: Expungement & Sealing', which direct the petitioner to file the Application for Waiver of Court Fees and describe it as a separate form. The Illinois memo independently records the statutory hook at 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(d)(1), which requires no fee where a Rule 298 order has been obtained.
rule298Treatment.doNotBindAsAGeneratedFilingDetail: Rule 298 is authority. It must never be bound to a component as a document to be generated, filled or delivered to a participant. Nothing is filed that is 'a Rule 298'.

whatActuallyConsumesTheAuthority.theFormTheRuleRequires: FW-CIV Application, ATJ 601.9 (08/25), Application for Waiver of Court Fees (Civil) — the participant-completed instrument, and the only Rule 298 artifact a packet can contain.
whatActuallyConsumesTheAuthority.theProceduralComponentsThatConsumeIt: The nine fee_waiver components listed below. Each is conditional on the participant being unable to pay the county filing fee.

theCourtOutputTheStatuteKeysOn.ruleBasis: Rule 298(c)(3) requires an order deciding an Application to use the approved Order form.
theCourtOutputTheStatuteKeysOn.statutoryRelevance: 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(d)(1) waives the expungement or sealing filing fee where a Rule 298 order has been obtained, which is what the Illinois memo's component notes record. The order is therefore legally load-bearing for the packet's fee narrative.
theCourtOutputTheStatuteKeysOn.packetTreatment: It is judge-facing. The court issues it; the participant does not complete it. It must NOT be added as a participant packet component, and its absence from the nine components is correct rather than a gap. Recorded expressly so no later worker adds it on the strength of the statutory reference.

resolvedDocumentIdentity.suiteDesignationNote: FW-CIV is the Illinois Courts suite and file-naming prefix; ATJ 601.9 is the identifier printed on the form itself. Both are official; neither is a rule number.
resolvedDocumentIdentity.officialTitle: Application for Waiver of Court Fees (Civil)
resolvedDocumentIdentity.officialTitleBasis: the retained binary's own document-information /Title entry
resolvedDocumentIdentity.printedCaptionOnTheFace: APPLICATION FOR WAIVER OF COURT FEES (CIVIL) / IN THE STATE OF ILLINOIS, CIRCUIT COURT
resolvedDocumentIdentity.issuer: Illinois Supreme Court Commission on Access to Justice, approved by the Illinois Supreme Court
resolvedDocumentIdentity.issuerBasisOnTheFace: the retained binary's /Author entry reads 'Commission on Access to Justice', and every page footer reads 'This form is approved by the Illinois Supreme Court and is required to be used in all Illinois Circuit Courts. Forms are free at ilcourts.info/forms.'
resolvedDocumentIdentity.roleDetail: A supporting application filed alongside the expungement or sealing request where the participant cannot pay the filing fee. It is not the primary filing, not an order and not instructions.
resolvedDocumentIdentity.signatoryDetail: The signature block reads: 'Under 735 ILCS 5/1-109, my signature means that: 1) Everything in this document is true and correct, or I have been informed or I believe it to be true and correct, and 2) I understand that making a false statement on this form is perjury and has penalties provided by law.' It offers two mutually exclusive checkboxes, 'I am completing this form for myself' and 'I am a lawyer completing this form on behalf of a client'. Rule 298(a) additionally permits signature by another person having knowledge of the facts where the applicant is a minor or an incompetent adult. There is no notary and no jurat; the certification is under 735 ILCS 5/1-109 rather than an oath.
resolvedDocumentIdentity.currentnessBasis: The retained copy at sha256 b2da395f5ba53eb3cec6bbd39a746f2152bf7f84987ea5f4b5c511ada17337f5 and 1,051,549 bytes is byte-identical to the binary the Illinois Courts publish today, confirmed 2026-08-07. The approved-forms library records the FW-CIV suite as Approved 08/2025 and the form's own footer reads (08/25) on all four pages. No newer circuit-court revision exists.
resolvedDocumentIdentity.revisionOnTheFace: (08/25), printed in the footer of every page beside 'ATJ 601.9' and 'Page n of 4'
resolvedDocumentIdentity.statewideScopeBasis: Illinois Supreme Court Rule 10-101(c): 'Standardized court forms may be used by any litigant or lawyer whenever they are applicable. All courts must accept standardized court forms.' Rule 10-101(d) further forbids any court from maintaining, creating or disseminating alternate forms seeking the same remedy, or requiring or encouraging any other form. The form's own footer states it is required to be used in all Illinois Circuit Courts.
resolvedDocumentIdentity.mandatoryFormNote: Mandatory as to form, not as to filing. The nine components are conditional: a participant who can pay the fee files nothing. Where the waiver route is used, this is the form and no county substitute is permitted.
resolvedDocumentIdentity.officialUrlBasis: corroborating official reading on 2026-08-07; the controlling identity is the retained adopted asset, and these URLs are recorded so the identity can be re-verified later

similarlyNamedDifferentRole.mustNotBeBoundReason: The FW-CIV Application's own face says so: 'If your case is a criminal case, use the Application for Waiver of Criminal Court Assessments form.' That sentence is a trap in this context, because an expungement petition arises out of a criminal case while the petition itself is a civil proceeding under 735 ILCS 5/5-105. The official statewide expungement instructions resolve it by routing petitioners to the civil form. The Cook variant is additionally county-specific and must never be promoted to statewide.

binaryFindings.signatureFieldsNote: There is no digital-signature field. The signature is a typed or handwritten name in a text field, as the form's own instruction directs.

widgetVersusTerminalFieldDenominator.arithmetic: 121 fields, of which 7 are multi-widget: one 4-widget text field and six 2-widget checkboxes. 114 single-widget fields + 4 + 12 = 130 widgets.
widgetVersusTerminalFieldDenominator.warning: This is the field-count denominator hazard in its exact form. The family source-requirements scaffold records expectedFieldCount 121, which is the terminal-field count. An edition state-manifest fieldCount is a widget count and would be 130. Any field map keyed on one number while validating against the other will silently misalign by nine. Both numbers are recorded here so the ambiguity cannot survive.
widgetVersusTerminalFieldDenominator.caseNumberFieldNote: '4 - Case Number' repeats across all four pages, which is why it carries four widgets. A renderer must write it once and let all four widgets render, not treat them as four separate values.

binaryFindings.boxDefaultingNote: BleedBox, TrimBox and ArtBox are absent from every page dictionary and default to the CropBox under the PDF specification, which here equals the MediaBox. Recorded as absent-and-defaulting rather than as measured-present or as zero.
binaryFindings.nominalSize: US Letter, 8.5 in x 11 in at 72 points per inch, on all four pages
binaryFindings.javascriptNote: pdfinfo reports JavaScript: yes. Typical of an ATJ fillable form's field formatting and calculation logic. Flagged because a renderer that flattens or rewrites the form must decide what happens to it; that decision is not made here.
